---
title: T7 - Environmental seasonality
jupyter: python3
---

An individual’s dose through long-cycle transmission in the model is attenuated or amplified by a mechanism for seasonality. Seasonality can represent an attenuation of the likely constant shedding of individuals into the long-cycle vehicle; a temperature-dependent growth in the level of CFUs in the environmental pool; changes to the rates of decay or removal of CFU from the environment; or any other method of seasonal forcing. 


Here, seasonal bacterial growth adds CFUs to the environment from outside the model, 1 million a day on average, from none to 2 million and back twice a year: `ss.modify()` adds an `ss.seasonal()` amount to the shedding into the environment. A parameter of the disease can be seasonal instead, e.g. `ty.Typhoid(shedding_rate=ss.seasonal(mean=ss.perday(1.0), amplitude=0.9, peak='January'))` (or `decay_rate`, or `teer`).

```{python}
import starsim as ss
import typhoidsim as ty

# Define high-level simulation parameters
pars = dict(
    start    = 2000,          # Starting year
    dur      = ss.years(10),  # Duration of the simulation
    dt       = ss.days(1),    # Timestep of 1 day
    verbose  = 0,             # Do not print details of the run
)

# The population
ppl = ss.People(10_000)

# The disease, with reduced protection per infection `tppi`, and transmission only through the environment
typhoid = ty.Typhoid(tppi=0.1, exposure2contact_rate=0)

# Bacterial growth adds CFUs to the environment (long cycle CCVT), in a cycle of half a year
growth = ss.seasonal(mean=ss.perday(1e6), amplitude=1.0, period=ss.years(0.5))
bacterial_growth = ss.modify(typhoid.shedding, add=growth, name='bacterial_growth')

sim = ss.Sim(
    pars=pars,
    people=ppl,
    diseases=typhoid,
    interventions=bacterial_growth,
    )

sim.run()
sim.plot('typhoid_cfu')
```

### Attenuate the level of exposure by reducing the shedding rate into the environment

An intervention can change a parameter over time with `ss.modify()`. Here, sanitation reduces the shedding rate by 30% for the first half of each year, starting in 2005. The profile of the reduction over time is a Python function of the year, and the modifier multiplies the shedding rate by one minus it.

```{python}
import starsim as ss
import typhoidsim as ty

# Define high-level simulation parameters
pars = dict(
    start    = 2000,          # Starting year
    dur      = ss.years(10),  # Duration of the simulation
    dt       = ss.weeks(1),   # Timestep of 1 week
    verbose  = 0,             # Do not print details of the run
)

# The population
ppl = ss.People(50_000)

# The disease, with reduced protection per infection `tppi`,
# initial typhoid prevalence `init_prev`, preexisting
# population immunity `init_seroprev`, and transmission
# only through the environment
typhoid = ty.Typhoid(tppi=0.1, init_seroprev=0.8, init_prev=0.001, exposure2contact_rate=0)

# Modulates the level of CFUs in the environment by reducing the shedding rate from people to the environment,
# using a periodic rectangular pulse
def sanitation_efficacy(year, period=1.0, width=0.5, max_efficacy=0.3):
    """ The reduction in shedding: max_efficacy for the first `width` years of each `period` years """
    return (year % period < width) * max_efficacy

sanitation = ss.modify('typhoid.pars.shedding_rate', multiply=lambda sim: 1 - sanitation_efficacy(sim.t.now('year')), start=2005, name='sanitation')

sim = ss.Sim(
    pars=pars,
    people=ppl,
    diseases=typhoid,
    interventions=sanitation
    )

sim.run()
sim.plot('typhoid_cfu')
```

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

years = sim.t.yearvec
efficacy = sanitation_efficacy(years)*(years >= 2005) # The profile, from the start of the intervention

plt.figure()
plt.plot(sim.timevec, efficacy, label='Efficacy profile')
plt.plot(sim.timevec, 1 - efficacy, label='Relative shedding rate')

plt.axvline(x=ss.date(2005), color='k', ls='--')
plt.title('Seasonal shedding reduction')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```
